currentContext.expansion: CPIL is an asset-light commodity trading house and the annual report discloses no plant, capacity addition, commissioning or capex project of any kind. Expansion is framed entirely as market and segment expansion rather than physical build-out: the Company says it remains committed to expanding its market presence in imported coal trading through strategic sourcing, efficient logistics management and customer-oriented services, and intends to strengthen its coal market position by capitalising on industry demand and operational efficiencies. In metals it continues to evaluate opportunities in metal scrap and sponge iron trading, with diversification pursued selectively based on market opportunities. In agro, the Company reports it has undertaken measured efforts to re-establish the agro business by exploring modern technologies and advanced agro machinery, and continues to explore agricultural mechanisation through deployment of modern agricultural equipment, but states it remains watchful and will evaluate growth prospects as and when viable opportunities arise - no equipment purchase, site or timeline is named. There is no subsidiary, associate or joint venture, and no acquisition or new geography is disclosed. Capital allocation during the year ran the other way: the Company continued to reduce reliance on borrowed funds through repayment of bank loans.
